2005.clinched: Sakhir sprint race, 30 September 2005, final round
2005.note: The first GP2 championship was decided at a stand-alone meeting at Sakhir, the only round of 2005 that did not support a grand prix, and Rosberg won both races there. Heikki Kovalainen had led the standings for most of the year until a last-lap spin at Spa cost him a finish. Rosberg took pole in an unusual two-part qualifying session, led Alexandre Prémat and Kovalainen home in the feature race, then won the sprint on 30 September 2005 to settle it: the first driver to win both races of a GP2 weekend. Five wins in the second half of the season had turned it, and ART took the teams' title.

2006.clinched: Monza feature race, 9 September 2006, one race to spare (race 20 of 21)
2006.note: Hamilton's championship was confirmed by the stewards. He finished third in the Monza feature race on 9 September 2006, behind Giorgio Pantano and Nelson Piquet Jr., and was set to go into the sprint needing a single point; then Pantano lost the fastest-lap point for having set it under yellow flags at the Parabolica, it passed to Hamilton, and the title was beyond Piquet with a race still to run. Hamilton said afterwards that he would rather have won it on the track. It was his first season in the category, with five wins and thirteen podiums, and ART's second title in a row.

2007.clinched: Valencia sprint race, 30 September 2007, final round
2007.note: Glock began the last weekend of 2007 two points ahead of Lucas di Grassi and ended it a champion with a lights-to-flag win. The Valencia feature race was run on a drying track where the tyre call decided everything: Vitaly Petrov won it, Glock finished seventh, and di Grassi spun off shortly after switching to slicks, which left Glock needing only fourth place in the sprint. He started second, led into the first corner and won it on 30 September 2007. He took the title on 88 points to di Grassi's 77, the first champion of the series not driving for ART Grand Prix.

2008.clinched: Monza feature race, 13 September 2008, one race to spare (race 19 of 20)
2008.note: Pantano arrived at Monza eleven points ahead of Bruno Senna, took pole to stretch it to thirteen, and then lost the race he was leading. As the track dried he pitted for slicks and rejoined narrowly in front, then cut a chicane trying to get temperature into the tyres, drew a drive-through penalty and dropped to tenth and out of the points. Lucas di Grassi won. Senna finished fifth, which was not enough, so the championship was settled on 13 September 2008 with the sprint race still to come. Pantano was the series' first Italian champion, in his seventh season in it, and all four of his wins that year were feature races.

2009.clinched: Monza sprint race, 13 September 2009, two races to spare (round 9 of 10)
2009.note: Hülkenberg won the championship in his first season in the category, and won it in the Monza sprint race on 13 September 2009 by finishing third while Vitaly Petrov failed to score enough to stay in the fight. Giedo van der Garde had taken the feature race the day before. Hülkenberg was close to unbeatable on Saturdays: his season turned at the Nürburgring with pole and a double win, and he added feature-race victories in Hungary, Valencia and Portimão. He was the third driver to take the series as a rookie, after Nico Rosberg and Lewis Hamilton, and ART won the teams' title.

2010.clinched: Monza sprint race, 12 September 2010, two races to spare (round 9 of 10)
2010.note: Maldonado hit the wall three times over the Monza weekend and won the championship anyway. He crashed out of the feature race on the Saturday, which Sam Bird won, and crashed again in the sprint on 12 September 2010, but Sergio Pérez could finish no better than thirteenth and that settled it with two races still to run. The title had been built on six consecutive feature-race wins, a series record, by a driver who had managed four wins in his three previous seasons. He finished sixteen points clear of Pérez, and Rapax took the teams' championship in its first year under the name.

2011.clinched: Spa-Francorchamps feature race, 27 August 2011, three races to spare (round 8 of 9)
2011.note: Grosjean settled the 2011 championship at Spa on 27 August, coming through from seventh on the grid to third in the feature race while his title rival Giedo van der Garde crashed out of it. That was his ninth podium of the season and it left three races still to run. He had been placed at DAMS to rebuild a team that had not been near a title since the series began, and he won the GP2 Asia championship the same year: a double that took him back to a Formula 1 seat after two years away. The Monza finale mattered only for the teams' championship.

2012.clinched: Marina Bay feature race, 22 September 2012, one race to spare (round 12 of 12)
2012.note: Valsecchi led the championship in the spring, lost it to Luiz Razia in mid-season, and took it back with a home win at Monza. At Singapore on 22 September 2012 he qualified sixth to Razia's ninth and finished fourth in the feature race with Razia fifth, which made the following day's sprint irrelevant. Max Chilton won the race, the first GP2 feature run at Marina Bay. Valsecchi ended the year on 247 points to Razia's 222, having won three of the four races in Bahrain to open the season, and DAMS retained the title it had won with Romain Grosjean.

2013.clinched: Yas Marina feature race, 2 November 2013, one race to spare (round 11 of 11)
2013.note: Leimer went to Abu Dhabi seven points ahead of Sam Bird with five drivers still mathematically in it, and settled the championship in the feature race on 2 November 2013 with fourth place. Bird stalled from second on the grid and recovered only to tenth, worth a single point. Alexander Rossi won the race from pole, ahead of Jolyon Palmer. It was Leimer's fourth season in the category and it was won on consistency rather than speed: feature-race wins in Malaysia, Bahrain and at Monza, and a top-six finish in every race from the Nürburgring onwards. He took the title by twenty points.

2014.clinched: Sochi feature race, 11 October 2014, three races to spare (round 11 of 12)
2014.note: Palmer won the Sochi feature race on 11 October 2014 and the championship with it, holding off Mitch Evans over the closing laps with Raffaele Marciello third. Stoffel Vandoorne had taken pole and led early but lost the race by staying out when the safety car came in; Palmer's nearest rival in the standings, Felipe Nasr, served two drive-through penalties for track limits and finished eighteenth. Palmer had 256 points when he took the title, already a record for a GP2 season, and finished the year on 276, from four wins, eight more podiums, nineteen consecutive points finishes and a score in twenty of the twenty-two races. He was the first British champion since Lewis Hamilton.

2015.clinched: Sochi sprint race, 11 October 2015, four races to spare (round 9 of 11)
2015.note: Vandoorne had been expected to settle it on the Saturday, but Alexander Rossi won the feature race and made him wait a day. In the Sunday sprint on 11 October 2015 he only had to finish ahead of Rossi, and fourth place after a three-way scrap with Raffaele Marciello and Pierre Gasly did it, with four races still to run. Richie Stanaway won the race behind the safety car. Vandoorne was never headed in the standings all year, finishing outside the top two only once in the first eight races, and took the title 108 points clear with five feature-race wins and twelve podiums.

2016.clinched: Yas Marina sprint race, 27 November 2016, final race of the season
2016.note: Gasly took pole at Yas Marina, won Saturday's feature race to move back ahead of his Prema team-mate Antonio Giovinazzi, then started the last GP2 race ever run from eighth on a reversed grid. He finished ninth and scored nothing; Giovinazzi could not reach the podium places, and the title was Gasly's by eight points, 219 in total. He had won at Silverstone, the Hungaroring, Spa and Abu Dhabi, and he was the second French champion of the series after Romain Grosjean. Prema took the teams' title in its first GP2 season.

2017.clinched: Jerez feature race, 7 October 2017, three races to spare
2017.note: Leclerc took his eighth pole of the season at Jerez, a record for the category, and won the feature race on 7 October 2017 to settle the championship with three races still to run. A safety car on lap 32, after Santino Ferrucci and Nobuharu Matsushita collided, wiped out his lead and left him defending on worn tyres; he beat his nearest rival Oliver Rowland to the line by 0.230 seconds. He had 247 points and six wins when he took it and finished the year on 282 with seven, a rookie champion, and the first driver to win the GP3 and Formula 2 titles in consecutive seasons.

2018.clinched: Yas Marina feature race, 24 November 2018, final round
2018.note: Russell needed eighth place under the lights at Yas Marina and won the race instead, his seventh victory of the season, which equalled Charles Leclerc's record for the category. He had arrived 41 points clear of Alexander Albon and added four more for pole. The start was chaos: he spun his wheels and lost the lead to Nyck de Vries, while Albon and Nicholas Latifi both stalled and Arjun Maini hit Latifi's stationary car. Russell took the lead back through the pit stops and controlled it. Albon recovered to fourteenth, which confirmed it, on 24 November 2018.

2019.clinched: Sochi feature race, 28 September 2019, three races to spare (round 11 of 12)
2019.note: De Vries needed to put 66 points between himself and Nicholas Latifi and did it in one afternoon: pole at Sochi, then the feature race win on 28 September 2019, with Latifi second behind him and Louis Delétraz third. That took the gap to 70 with three races left. He finished the season on 266 points, 52 clear, with twelve podiums and points in every race but the last two. It was his fifth year in the category and it took him to Formula E with Mercedes, where he won the world championship at the first attempt.

2020.clinched: Sakhir sprint race, 6 December 2020, final race of the season
2020.note: Schumacher went into the last race of 2020 fourteen points ahead of Callum Ilott and scored nothing in it, and it was still enough. He dived between Dan Ticktum and Jehan Daruvala at the start, nearly threw it away with a heavy lock-up at the second corner, lost pace, was called into the pit lane and rejoined to finish eighteenth. Ilott, needing a win, climbed to third and then fell back to tenth. Daruvala won the race. Schumacher finished the season on 215 points with two wins, the fourth Formula 2 champion after Charles Leclerc, George Russell and Nyck de Vries.

2021.clinched: Yas Marina sprint race 1, 11 December 2021, two races to spare
2021.note: Piastri only needed his team-mate Robert Shwartzman off the podium, and instead settled it himself. Starting tenth on a reversed grid in the first Abu Dhabi sprint on 11 December 2021, he gained four places on the opening lap and finished third behind Jehan Daruvala and Felipe Drugovich, which put the championship beyond a 55.5-point deficit. He had taken a fifth consecutive pole the day before. Piastri closed the year with the Sunday feature win, his sixth of the season, on 252.5 points with eleven podiums: a rookie champion, and his third title in three years after Formula Renault and Formula 3.

2022.clinched: Monza sprint race, 10 September 2022, three races to spare
2022.note: Drugovich won the 2022 title while standing in the pit lane. He had arrived at Monza 70 points clear with 78 still available, and his sprint race on 10 September ended at Turn 5 on the first lap when contact with Amaury Cordeel broke his suspension. It did not matter: Théo Pourchaire needed fifth place to keep the fight alive, ran wide trying to pass Liam Lawson for tenth, picked up a penalty and finished last. Jüri Vips won the race. Drugovich took five wins that season and finished more than a hundred points clear, the first Formula 2 champion MP Motorsport has had.

2023.clinched: Yas Marina feature race, 26 November 2023, final round
2023.note: Pourchaire was beaten by Frederik Vesti in qualifying, in the sprint and in the feature race at Yas Marina, and still won the championship. Vesti's sprint win took the fight to the last day for the first time since 2018; then on 26 November 2023 Pourchaire started fourteenth in the feature, gained nine places to finish fifth, and that was enough. Vesti came back to third and finished 11 points short, 203 to 192. Jack Doohan won the race. Pourchaire had only one win all year, in the opening Bahrain feature, but ten podiums across both formats, and he was ART's first champion since Nyck de Vries.

2024.clinched: Yas Marina feature race, 8 December 2024, final round
2024.note: Bortoleto arrived in Abu Dhabi half a point ahead of Isack Hadjar and left it champion. The sprint stretched that to four and a half; then in the feature race on 8 December 2024 he took the lead on the opening lap while Hadjar stalled from third on the grid and finished a lap down. Joshua Dürksen won the race, with Bortoleto second after passing Victor Martins around the outside of Turn 9, and Richard Verschoor third. Final points 214.5 to Hadjar's 192. It was a rookie season, and it made him the fourth driver to win F3 and F2 back to back.

2025.clinched: Lusail feature race, 30 November 2025, one round to spare (round 13 of 14)
2025.note: Fornaroli started the Qatar feature race from pole on 30 November 2025, was beaten off the line by Victor Martins, and spent 32 laps doing nothing risky at all behind him. Second place and the two points for pole put him on 211 to Jak Crawford's and Richard Verschoor's 170, with only Abu Dhabi left. He had to wait a few minutes for a stewards' investigation into Arvid Lindblad to clear before it was official. Four wins and five more podiums, with a top-eight finish in 23 of the 25 races, made him the fifth rookie champion in Formula 2 and the second Invicta driver in a row to take the title.
